summary: Standing steel lookout tower at the summit of Elmore Mountain in Elmore State Park, Lamoille County, VT; built 1939, active to 1974, NHLR-registered 1995.

facts.design: Steel lookout tower, 45 ft 9 in high (state report, 1938-40)
facts.agency: Vermont Dept. of Forests, Parks and Recreation

access.note: Hiking trails in Elmore State Park lead to the tower at the summit. A May 2, 2025 news article says Elmore Mountain would see shorter closures while railings were installed. No rental notice found. Sources do not address climbing the cab.

visit.trail_note: Hiking trails in Elmore State Park lead to the observation tower at the summit.

events.note: Built 1939: Wikipedia says the state built the observation tower the year after 1938; the register says a federal forestry task force completed the tower that year. A 1938-40 state report says a steel tower 45 ft 9 in was built with New England Forest Emergency funds, and a CCC cabin was being built.
Earliest staffing found: a 24 April 1958 Burlington Free Press item says Collins Parker was employed at the lookout tower on Elmore Mountain.
Register: the lookout remained active until 1974.
Registered November 24, 1995; nominated by Mark Haughwout, FFLA.
Interior cab railings installed at Elmore and Spruce Mountain towers in the 2025 work.
Shorter closures at Elmore Mountain while railings were installed; work expected to extend into spring 2026 (article posted May 2, 2025).

corrections.why: Wikipedia spells the county Lamoille. The register and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list use the misspelling Lemoille, which the record copied.

Wikipedia gives the summit as 2,608 ft (795 m) and places the tower atop the summit. The register lists 2,287 ft (697 m) for its site. The sources do not reconcile the two, so the editor should confirm before changing.

sources.title: Restoration project set to begin on Vt. fire towers

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia credits the state with building the tower the year after 1938; the register credits a federal forestry task force; the 1938-40 state report credits New England Forest Emergency funds and CCC work. Story reports all three.
Register gives 2,287 ft (697 m); Wikipedia gives the summit as 2,608 ft (795 m). Not resolved; story says so.

notes_for_editor: Brief lat/lon 44.5287, -72.544517 is the register's point. The FFLA list gives 44.52639, -72.54603, roughly 250 m apart. UVM text says the summit is 795 feet, which looks like a units slip; Wikipedia gives 795 m. Height 13.9 m is converted from the 1938-40 report's 45 ft 9 in. Brief 'Lemoille' county is a misspelling; correction proposed. Not searched: a snippet says the tower is decommissioned but still standing (not read). Page reads: 4 new (Wikipedia, UVM, NHLR, Forest Lookouts); FFLA list and 2025 PDF reused from earlier fetches. Staffing after 1974 not found.
